name: Motorized Bicycle
description: DC law has no electric bicycle category: an e-bike is a motorized bicycle, with pedals, wheels at least 16 inches across and a motor that can't propel it past 20 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels at least 16 inches in diameter, a post-mounted seat for each rider, and fully operative pedals
Its motor can't propel it faster than 20 mph on level ground; the definition sets no wattage limit and draws no line between a throttle and pedal assist

Operated by its motor past 20 mph it is a motor-driven cycle, and its rider needs a driver's license; past 30 mph it is a motorcycle, and the rider needs a motorcycle endorsement; riding one faster than 20 mph is a $100 infraction
restrictions.citation: 18 DCMR 9901.1, as amended by D.C. Law 19-290

restrictions.rule: The definition predates the three e-bike classes and doesn't say whether a Class 3's 28 mph pedal assist counts as being operated by its motor
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration, inspection or insurance
A new one sold for use on streets must carry a red rear reflector
May ride DC's off-street shared-use paths, since a 2022 DDOT rule repealed their ban on motorized bicycles
On National Park Service land in DC, such as Rock Creek Park, federal rules apply instead: e-bikes ride only where the superintendent allows them
